events.note:
Funeral services were conducted for Allan Martens on Wednesday, December 11, at Zion Lutheran Church of Canistota, S. Dak. at 2:00 P.M. Rev. P. R. Albrecht was in charge of the service. A trio consisting of mrs. Charles Jarratt, Mrs. Gale Snow and Mrs. Henry Anderson sang, "The Old Rugged Cross" and "Heaven Is My Home," accompanied by Mrs. P. R. Albrecht.

Honorary pallbearers were Messrs. Francis Tusha, Leo Bartling, Walter Scharffenberg, Henry Biehlo, Ewald Neumann and Henry Scharffenberg.

Active pallbearers were Messrs. Walter Stevens, Wlater Turrell, Walter Johnke, Alton Wuertzer, John Teide and Alvin Teckleberg.

Mr. Allan Martens passed away suddenly on Sunday afternoon of a heart attack at the farm 6 miles east of Canistota. He had gone into the pasture to free some sheep from snow drifts when he called for help. He had expired before help could reach him at about 4:45 P.M. His age at death was 52 years, 8 months and 10 days.

Allan Paul Martens was born on March 28, 1911 at Bridgewater, S. Dak. He was the son of Mr. Henry Martens and his wife Marie, nee Koch. He was baptized on August 12, 1911 at Zion Lutheran Church of Bridgewater. Here he was also confirmed by Pastor Janzig on June 13, 1926.

He was united in marriage with Erna, nee Zelmer on March 3, 1935 at Bridgewater. To this union four children were born, but the first son died at birth. Thre children survive their father.

Mr. Martens worked for other people on the farm until 1936 when he began farming for himself some 8 miles northwest of Bridgewater. They farmed there for 14 years, then in 1951 farmed about 5 miles northeast of Canistota. In 1958 they moved to the present farm.

Bereaved who morur his loss incliude his widow, Mrs. Erna Martens of Canistota, a son, Dennis of Vermillion, and two daughters, Mrs. Joan Tarrell of Canistota and Sharal Martens, who is at home. Six sisters and one brother also survive. They are Mrs. Anna Gill of Eugene, Oregon, Mrs. Amanda Rupkalvis of Rochester, Minn., Mrs. Nora Heiman of Bridgewater, Mrs. Esther Nelson of Washington, Mrs. Marie Wipf of Bridgewater, Mrs. Hazel Breeding of Las Vegas, Nevada, and Mr. Edmund Martens of Golden, Colorado. Six brothers and one sister precede him in death. He also leaves two grandchildren and many other relatives and friends.

The Canistota Clipper
Thursday, Dec. 12, 1963
